segments.name: Traditional Business
segments.description: Publishes newspapers and websites covering California and Arizona news, produces specialized information publications, and serves as a public notice advertising representative.
segments.evidence: The Company's Traditional Business is one reportable segment and the other is Journal Technologies which includes Journal Technologies, Inc. and Journal Technologies (Canada) Inc.

segments.name: Journal Technologies
segments.description: Supplies case management software systems and related products to courts, justice agencies, and other government customers in the U.S. and internationally.
segments.evidence: Journal Technologies, Inc. ("Journal Technologies"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, supplies case management software systems and related products to courts, prosecutor and public defender offices, probation departments and other justice agencies, including administrative law organizations, city and county governments and bar associations.

revenueModel.text: The Traditional Business earns subscription, advertising and service fees from readers, advertisers and attorneys, while Journal Technologies earns license, maintenance, hosting, consulting and public e-filing/payment fees, almost all from government agencies.
revenueModel.evidence: Journal Technologies earns revenues from license, maintenance and support fees paid by customers to use its software products; hosting services; consulting fees paid by customers for installation, implementation and training services; and fees generated by the use of secure websites through which the general public can pay traffic citations and e-file cases.
